questions.question: You get a 'KeyError: target' when running df['target']. What is the best prompt to send the contest AI?
options: Here is my 200-line data loading script, what is wrong?
KeyError: target on df['target']. How do I list all column names in a pandas DataFrame?
Fix my code so it doesn't give errors.
What is a KeyError?
questions.explanation: Short and specific wins. Paste only the error and the line, then ask for the exact thing you need (how to list columns). Generic questions get generic answers.

questions.question: The contest AI has input and output length limits. What does this mean for how you write prompts?
options: Paste your full script so the AI has all the context it needs.
Ask one large question that covers everything at once.
Be specific. Paste only the few lines that relate to your question.
Always ask in bullet points to save space.
questions.explanation: Limits force you to be precise. Paste the minimum code that shows the problem, and ask one specific question. You get better answers and waste less of your input budget.

questions.question: Which of these is a good use of the contest AI?
options: Write me a neural network that classifies my dataset.
My score is 0.65, how do I get to 0.80?
What does StratifiedKFold do differently from KFold? One sentence.
Is my whole approach correct?
questions.explanation: Asking for a quick concept clarification (with 'one sentence') is perfect. The AI can answer this precisely. The other options are too vague or ask the AI to do your work for you.

questions.question: While studying, what is the best way to use a full AI tool so you are prepared for the contest?
options: Ask it to write all your code so you see correct examples.
Try the problem yourself first, then ask the AI to explain WHY your code fails, not HOW to fix it.
Skip the AI entirely while studying.
Ask the AI to rate your code quality.
questions.explanation: Building a mental model matters most. If you just copy AI solutions, you won't be able to work with the contest's limited AI. Try first, then use AI to understand the gap.

questions.question: You are confused about what log-loss measures. According to the lesson's prompt patterns, a good prompt is:
options: Explain log-loss in full detail with examples.
The task says minimize log-loss. My model outputs class probabilities. What value is 'good' for a 3-class problem?
Here is my training loop, is the loss going down correctly?
What is entropy?
questions.explanation: Give context (3-class, probabilities) and ask one specific thing (what counts as a good value). This gets a targeted answer in few words.
